researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Did trilateral missile-warning information sharing operate on an ongoing basis after the Camp David commitments?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Document pre-August-2023 information-sharing arrangements and operational limits.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Find dated US/Japan/ROK defense ministry reports of operational exchanges, exercises, and continuity.
researchPlan.attributionAlternatives: Pre-existing US bilateral alliances and independent Japan-ROK reconciliation.
researchPlan.costRequirement: Identify direct defense coordination costs and concessions in comparable units.

observedEvidence.finding: August 18, 2023: US, Japan and South Korea committed to activate trilateral real-time DPRK missile-warning data sharing. November 2023: ministers reported final-stage testing. December 19, 2023: all three governments announced full activation following operational tests. This is a documented change from prior separate US bilateral data-sharing arrangements, not proof of unilateral US influence.

baseline.description: United States shared DPRK missile-warning information separately with Japan and South Korea; the new trilateral real-time mechanism had not yet been fully activated.

followup.description: Trilateral real-time missile-warning mechanism fully activated according to US and Japanese defense ministries.

observedEvidence.caveat: Official ministry statements corroborate activation but are not independent operational performance data. Shared Japanese and Korean agency, duration of operation, costs and counterfactual remain unresolved.

measurementQuality.reason: Qualitative pre/post operational activation documented by multiple governments, but not a matched quantitative outcome series or independently validated operational performance.

sourceAudit.notes: US and Japanese defense ministry releases and US Pacific Command statements located and reviewed for dated operational activation claim. Full independent claim-level audit (reviewer, publication-date check, definition reconciliation) remains pending.

researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Did CEPA change eligible product trade volumes or tariff use compared with a defensible pre-2022 baseline?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Collect matched pre-CEPA product-level trade, tariff, and demand data.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Collect comparable customs tariff utilization and trade quantities for 2022 onward.
researchPlan.attributionAlternatives: Energy prices, global trade rebound, exchange rates and UAE demand.
researchPlan.costRequirement: Measure tariff revenue forgone, adjustment costs and bilateral distributional effects.

observedEvidence.caveat: Indian fiscal-year figures; FY2020-21 was pandemic-affected, and trade prices/volumes and broader recovery confound attribution. This is nominal gross trade, not net benefit. FY2021-22 pre-agreement trade was already USD 72.9 billion, showing substantial recovery before CEPA entered into force; avoid treating FY2020-21 as a representative unaffected baseline.

preAgreementContext.note: This fiscal year preceded CEPA entry into force on May 1, 2022; nominal bilateral trade had already recovered sharply from pandemic-era FY2020-21.

measurementQuality.reason: Aggregate nominal merchandise trade in matching units is observed, but pre-period pandemic distortion, composition and price effects, counterfactual and independent outcome validation remain unresolved.

evidenceAuditMethodology: Source-identified event records are not independently verified causal influence. Gate statuses indicate research coverage, not outcomes or influence. Empty gate means unassessed, not zero. Each sphere is reviewed against the same six gates.
researchPlanMethodology: Pre-registered research questions and source categories. Planned research is not a completed evidence audit. Never promote planned outcomes into measurements.
observationPolicy: Documented observation is not attributable influence. Only matched periods/definitions may support before-after differences; no cross-case ranking. Context from earlier initiatives must be disclosed.
measurementQualityPolicy: Measurement readiness is separate from research activity, source identification, and diplomatic influence. The five checks must all pass before a candidate can be called a comparable outcome measurement; even then causal attribution is a separate gate.
sourceAuditPolicy: No URL is marked independently verified merely because it is listed. Source access, exact claim, publication date, matched definitions and reviewer must be recorded. Missing audit remains pending; no inferred influence.
